findings.message: Terminal-state guard reads status before acquiring SELECT FOR UPDATE on the RedemptionRequest — two concurrent webhooks can both pass the guard and double-apply.
findings.manualAction: Add a SELECT FOR UPDATE lock on the RedemptionRequest before the terminal-state guard check, or use a DB-level unique constraint on (redemption_request_id, status) transitions.

findings.message: Unchecked cast chain on XTRM API response — NPE if nested keys (data, balance, amount) are absent from response.
findings.manualAction: Add null-safe navigation for each nested key before casting. Throw a typed domain exception on absent fields.

findings.message: maxInFlight check performed before acquiring wallet SELECT FOR UPDATE lock — concurrent submissions can both pass the in-flight guard.
findings.manualAction: Move the inFlight count check to after the wallet lock is acquired.

findings.message: Math.abs(UUID.hashCode()) used as IssuerTransactionId — hash collisions can produce duplicate IDs for different UUIDs.
findings.manualAction: Use a deterministic, collision-free ID derived from the UUID (e.g. truncated hex or a sequence).

findings.message: Signing secret defaults to empty string — no startup alerting if misconfigured. Blank secret silently disables HMAC validation.
findings.manualAction: Add an @EventListener(ApplicationReadyEvent.class) that logs ERROR and optionally throws if both signing secrets are blank.

findings.message: Repository injected directly into controller — entity construction and DB access belong in the service layer.
findings.manualAction: Move webhook event entity construction into RedemptionWebhookService.

findings.message: Throws raw RuntimeException on XTRM API error — callers cannot distinguish vendor errors from programming errors.
findings.manualAction: Define and throw a typed VendorIntegrationException.

findings.message: RestClient exchange returns a potentially-null body that is immediately dereferenced.
findings.manualAction: Add null check on RestClient response body before accessing nested fields.

findings.message: Pageable.unpaged() loads ALL client catalog configs from DB — unbounded query on large tenants.
findings.fix: Scoped config query to page item IDs using findByClientIdAndRedemptionCatalogItemIdIn.

findings.message: computeNextBatchDate re-queried settingsRepository — duplicate DB call when settings already loaded.
findings.fix: Load settings once per submission; pass BatchCadence directly to computeNextBatchDate(BatchCadence).

findings.message: log.error redundantly included e.getMessage() as placeholder arg alongside Throwable — cleaned to single-arg pattern.
log.error in validateHmac catch block logged only e.getMessage() — no stack trace captured.
findings.fix: Changed to log.error("[step=webhook-hmac-error]", e) to capture full stack trace.

findings.message: In-flight count check before wallet lock in submitPersonalRedemption — same race as submitCompanyRedemption.
findings.manualAction: Move inFlight check after wallet SELECT FOR UPDATE in both submission paths.

findings.message: findOrCreateSettings has a create-race — two concurrent first-access requests can both pass the findByClientId empty check and try to insert.
findings.manualAction: Add a DB unique constraint on (client_id) for tenant_redemption_settings, or use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

classificationRules.blockingThreshold: severity critical/high AND confidence >= 0.70 AND not alreadyHandled
classificationRules.advisoryThreshold: severity medium/low OR confidence < 0.70 OR alreadyHandled

findings.summary: Vendor dispatch runs before PROCESSING state is durably committed
findings.details: dispatchItem sets PROCESSING and calls orchestrationService.dispatch inside the same REQUIRES_NEW transaction. If the JVM dies or DB commit fails after the vendor call succeeds, the request reverts to RESERVED and the next batch run re-dispatches — causing a duplicate payout. There is no committed outbox or dispatchAttempt record protecting the external side effect.
findings.tierReason: severity=high, confidence=0.88 (≥ 0.70), alreadyHandled=false — no outbox or committed dispatch record protects vendor call
findings.recommendation: Persist a durable PROCESSING+dispatchAttempt record (or outbox row) first and commit it, then perform the vendor call in a separate non-transactional step using the persisted stable idempotency key.

findings.summary: XTRM IssuerTransactionId collapses 128-bit UUID to a collision-prone 32-bit hash
findings.details: Math.abs(request.getId().hashCode()) produces a 32-bit integer. Collisions become realistic at production volume and would cause XTRM to deduplicate or misattribute transfers. Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) also returns a negative value.
findings.tierReason: severity=high, confidence=0.82 (≥ 0.70), alreadyHandled=false — Math.abs(hashCode()) still in place
findings.recommendation: Use the full redemption UUID string (or a ULID/prefixed version) as IssuerTransactionId and persist it before dispatch for reconciliation.

findings.summary: Signed webhook can settle any PROCESSING redemption without vendor-channel validation
findings.details: The controller loads the redemption by ID and passes only a boolean completion/failure to the service. There is no check that the path vendor matches the request's expected settlement channel. A valid Xoxoday HMAC signature on a payload naming an XTRM cash redemption UUID would complete or fail that redemption.
findings.tierReason: severity=high, confidence=0.80 (≥ 0.70), alreadyHandled=false — no vendor vs request category/channel check
findings.recommendation: Persist expected vendor on dispatch; in webhook processing reject callbacks where vendor does not match the request's settlement channel.
